items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Rodger Ray was not there because Sid Weiss had pulled a trick on him.

ctx.x: The trumpet chair had been left open for me and the band had worked in the club two weeks before I returned. The club was located at 152nd East 55th Street. But Rodger Ray was not there because Sid Weiss had pulled a trick on him. Rodger's voice was not as good as he thought it was and when Sid heard him sing, and he knew that Rodger did not belong to the musicians union because he was not a musician, he reported him and a union delegate came to the club and told Rodger he could not work, because he was not a…

Sid promised Rodger that he would take charge of the orchestra until I arrived and Rodger was supposed to have his salary collected by Sid and given to him because he was the one that had found the job and formed th band.

and formed the band. But as Rodger could not go into the local, the owner of the club cut his salary off completely. The club was run by a fellow named Oscar who had been the head waiter at Cafe Uptown when it opened in 1940. The orchestra was playing more commercial numbers than jazz because that was what the owner wanted. Business was not good and within two weeks after I had joined the band, the place was closed. We did a radio show/that was the end of Rodger Ray's dream of being a singer and band leader.
